other_failure_modes.name: Cross-validation data leakage
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes imputation statistics (like the median) and fits categorical encoders on the entire training dataset before splitting it into cross-validation folds. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the validation performance estimates overly optimistic.

other_failure_modes.name: Retaining high-cardinality raw features
other_failure_modes.description: The agent extracts useful components from features like dates or IDs, but fails to drop the original raw columns. If these raw strings are passed to tree-based models as categorical features, their high cardinality can lead to severe memory issues and overfitting.

summary: The agent provides a structurally sound pipeline with cross-validation and feature engineering, but fails to respect temporal ordering by using a shuffled K-Fold split on time-sensitive data. Additionally, it leaks validation set statistics into the training folds during imputation and encoding, and applies a naive, unweighted ensemble strategy.
